# Agentic Guardians

> Your AI agent is already out there. Do you know what it's doing right now? Agentic Guardians answers that question. It is the runtime trust layer for AI agents. It scores your agent's behaviour before every action runs. It doesn't read prompts. It can't be persuaded. Every block is signed (Ed25519). Anyone can verify it. AI trust you can prove.

Every agent has a rhythm. Agentic Guardians learns it. When the rhythm breaks, the action stops before it runs. It watches what an agent does, never what it's told, so a prompt can't talk it round. We built it for small and mid-sized companies that are adopting AI fast, often without a security team. Stage: private beta.

## What it is

- The runtime trust layer for AI agents. It checks each action before it runs.
- Reads agent actions: file reads, API calls, shell commands, database queries. Never prompts or tokens.
- Engine: a statistical behavioural model of each agent's normal action sequences. No language model in the decision path. No rules to write.
- Runs on CPU. No GPU needed. Stays local. No cloud round-trip.
- For each action: allow, pause for a person to review, or block.
- Every block is signed (Ed25519). Anyone can verify it. Each block leaves a Detection Certificate: what was stopped, and why.
- Designed to align with NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, ISO/IEC 27001 and GDPR.

## The problem

- Agents act on their own, at machine speed: they read files, call APIs, query databases and run commands. Nobody is watching them yet.
- Agents drift. They make things up. They get weaponized. Then they act.
- A compromised agent doesn't look compromised. It isn't a break-in. It's a takeover from the inside. You may never know it happened.
- It doesn't take an attack. An agent can misread its instructions and act, sure of itself, on the wrong idea.
- Today's tools read prompts, check policies, or find out afterwards. None of them stop the action before it runs.
- The stakes: mistakes in payments, code, personnel records, legal work and health administration, faster than a person can step in. Some break GDPR, the EU AI Act or a contract.

## How it works

1. Learn: watches an agent's actions and learns its normal sequences.
2. Check: before each action runs, scores it against everything that came before.
3. Act: allow, pause, or block.
4. Prove: sign every block (Ed25519). Anyone can verify it.

Example: a payments agent always runs read_file → match_ledger → write_report. One day it tries an http.post to an account it has never paid. Agentic Guardians blocks the action before it runs and issues a signed Detection Certificate. Nothing is sent.

## Why we win: not AI watching AI

- Who guards the guardians? Most tools that watch agents are AI themselves: same architecture, same attack surface, same language. A prompt injection that fools the agent can reach the guard too.
- You cannot ask a corrupted process to report its own corruption. An AI watching an AI is just another alignment problem.
- Agentic Guardians doesn't process tokens. It doesn't read prompts, so a prompt can't reach it. There's nothing for an injection to talk to.
- It watches sequences of actions at the system level, using statistical models, not language models. CPU, not GPU.
- A compromised agent can say all the right things. It can't fake its rhythm.
- Filters read the attacker's language. Logs tell you afterwards. People can't keep up with machine speed.
- You don't need to understand the maths. You just need to check the signature.
- Light enough for a small company to run. Leaves the records regulated work needs.

## Why now

- Every major AI company is racing to make agents deployable at scale. The thing blocking adoption is trust.
- Everyone wants agents. Almost nobody trusts them yet. As companies hand work to agents, they lose the people who would have caught a rogue one.
- Nobody has solved trust with maths yet. We've spent over a decade on the maths it needs (see the IEEE Access 2020 research below).
- The window is now.

## Investors

- Stage: private beta. The engine works end to end: it learns each agent's baseline, blocks before execution, and signs every block. We're onboarding our first teams ourselves.
- Why we built it: Armine set up his own agent and realised he'd be giving it blind access to his world. The CTOs and engineers he asked said the same: the gains are real, so they sign off, but they sign off nervous. Ghazaros had spent years catching fraud by how it behaves, not by what it says. Agents need the same.
